prompts:
Context: A team is designing an inference service that accepts requests from several client applications. The service receives short bursts of traffic as well as periods with few active users. Each request contains a prompt and asks the model to generate a bounded response. Engineers need to compare different configurations using the same inputs and sampling settings. The deployment uses a gateway in front of a model server and collects metrics during each experiment. The gateway can admit a limited number of active requests and rejects extra requests at capacity. The team measures time to first content, end to end completion time, and successful output tokens per second. Several GPUs can run independent model replicas or cooperate on a single model using tensor parallelism. Tensor parallelism requires communication between devices during model execution. The speed of the interconnect and the size of the model can change the resulting tradeoffs. A small model might fit entirely on one device while a larger model can require multiple devices. Workload concurrency influences batching, resource use, throughput, and the time individual users wait. The experiment should record failed requests and should avoid treating missing token counts as zero. The input prompts, output limits, random sampling, software versions, and hardware must be documented. Each trial uses warmup requests before measuring so that initialization is not mistaken for steady behavior. All raw request records are retained so that summary statistics can be audited and recalculated. Percentiles calculated from a small number of requests may vary between repeated trials. The rental cost of a two GPU host continues even when a single model uses only one of the devices. Storage, network traffic, model downloads, setup, and idle time contribute to the actual amount paid. The team should distinguish estimated steady state compute cost from the final provider invoice. Charts should label the units and explain whether a value is an average of trials or a pooled statistic. The serving endpoint has no public authentication, so access is limited to the local host. If a request is interrupted or a stream ends early, the client records it as a failure. Engineers should not conclude that an observed difference is caused by one mechanism without further tests.
